original_test_intent: Validate each approved USB 2.0 and USB 3.x physical port path, including its hubs and MCU endpoints, enumerates the intended fixture at the required negotiated speed and completes an approved functional data exchange without resets or errors.
original_method: Select by row/variant; map chassis receptacle through controller/root port/hubs to MCU and fixture VID:PID/serial/interface/driver; operator connects the approved device; collect complete `lsusb -tv` and descriptors plus kernel events; prove SuperSpeed and high-speed paths on the correct ports at engineering-approved rates; where function exceeds enumeration, run a bounded non-destructive transfer/control transaction; preserve disconnect/reset/error counters and do not reset devices or reuse firmware-flash steps.
manual_activity: An operator identifies and connects the approved fixture to each physical USB port; automation cannot establish chassis-port identity unaided.
required_inputs: Unique identity resolution for the duplicated code
USB controller/root-port/internal/external hub/MCU/chassis-port topology and population matrix
Fixture cable/device VID:PID/product/serial/interface/class and supported USB generation
Expected per-port negotiated speed, descriptor/configuration and any safe functional transaction/error limits
safety_requirements: Select by row/variant and never execute same-code firmware-flash instructions
Bind each physical port to the logical bus path before judging output
Use approved fixtures and read-only enumeration unless a bounded transaction is separately authorized
Preserve complete descriptor/tree/kernel evidence and stop on repeated resets, overcurrent, wrong device, link downgrade or errors
Do not reset/rebind devices or retry automatically
agent_execution_scope: Validate USB topology, fixture identities and owner-approved speed/function matrix
Collect complete bus tree, descriptors, negotiated speeds and error events after operator actions
Run only a supplied non-destructive functional query if approved and report facts without verdict
Do not manipulate cables, flash firmware, reset/rebind devices, clear logs or infer missing criteria
engineer_actions: Resolve duplicate-code ownership while preserving both rows
Approve port/hub/MCU map, fixture and per-port speed/function oracle
Review physical plus software evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsusb -t`/`lsusb` address enumeration and negotiated topology only; `head` can hide the target and errors, and no physical-port binding or functional transaction is provided.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After operator port/fixture confirmation, collect complete `lsusb -tv`, full descriptors and USB kernel events, then execute only any separately approved bounded functional query.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/10-minute estimates remain; USB2 480M and USB3 5Gbps are treated as historical suggestions pending the project port-generation matrix.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Test each labeled physical port with a traceable fixture, full logical path and approved negotiated-speed/function matrix.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds collision-safe selection, complete topology/descriptors, fixture identity, physical-port mapping, reset/error evidence and optional safe functional exchange.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic USB tree cannot prove every intended port, MCU path or actual function; the same code can otherwise dispatch a destructive firmware flash.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Hub sharing and cable quality affect negotiation; 5 Gbps is not appropriate for every USB3 generation, so project-specific rates are required.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must define which receptacles are USB2-only, USB3 Gen1/Gen2 or internally connected to the MCU, and whether enumeration is sufficient or a transfer/control function is mandatory per port.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and separation from row 2041 firmware flash
Complete timestamped `lsusb -tv`, descriptors and negotiated speed for each port
Approved functional transaction result plus kernel reset/disconnect/overcurrent/error evidence
Physical port photos/labels, discrepancies and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Wistron-HW-00484-V002 identifies both row 2041 M.2 Firmware-Flash and row 2203 USB2/3 Function Check. Row/hash/variant resolves this review, but code-only dispatch could perform the wrong and destructive operation. Current USB Procedure/Criteria are also TBD.

blocked_analysis.analysis: USB2/3 port and MCU function is identifiable. Topology, fixture, speeds and functional criteria are supplyable inputs.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2203 Wistron-HW-00484-V002: assign/approve a unique identity distinct from row 2041 M.2 Firmware-Flash; approve the chassis-port/controller/root-port/hub/MCU map and population, fixture cable/device VID:PID/serial/interface, per-port USB generation and negotiated-speed matrix, whether enumeration alone or a bounded functional transfer/control transaction is required, reset/disconnect/overcurrent/error limits and recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents destructive same-code misdispatch and converts TBD USB coverage into a physical-port-specific topology, speed and function contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: USB enumeration paths are dynamic and a hub can hide which chassis receptacle was exercised, so physical labeling and a known fixture are essential. Negotiated 480M/5000M proves link class but not data/control functionality, and not every port is necessarily SuperSpeed. The duplicate code is particularly hazardous because its other row flashes NVMe firmware. Composite identity and strict prohibition of cross-variant commands are therefore part of this case's safety evidence.
